doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Recorded vocals with Danko and an Italian choir
summary: They discuss his scat vocals on record with Harold Danko and singing 'Nature Boy' and 'I Got It Bad' with an Italian choir.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: You’ve recorded vocals. You and Harold Danko did a couple vocal things on a couple records, right?
Uh, I don’t know if we did on a record or we did on a DVD.
I was looking through your discography. You and Danko did a scat vocal on one record, a duo record that you did in the eighties, doing “Lady Be Good” or something.
Yeah, we did Lester Young’s solo on “Lady Be Good”, but [I don’t] remember doing it on a record, wow.
When we go through your discography, probably tomorrow, we’ll just touch on little things like that and see if [they] trigger any memories.

What I did do though, was an Italian pianist that I was working with some time, invited me to record, after the fact, with a choir that he was coaching in Italy, I think a thirty-voice choir, I don’t know if it was a church choir or what, but I got to the record date and put on the headphones and I heard a [imitates a sound] and things like that, and then background for [sings a melody].

Nature Boy. [I] said “I’m gonna sing that and not play it”. So I sang it and then there was a second one on “I Got It Bad . . .” which got me up [sings a melody in a higher register] and the engineer said: “my, you’re better than Chet Baker”, and I said “thanks a lot” but it wasn’t really good because [it was] a little bit pitchy-pitchy and things like that.
Well “I Got It Bad” has got to be one of hardest tunes to sing.
It was not easy but I have a proof of that some place. Every once in a while I, in the quiet of my chamber, I check it out with the earphones.
